patients.summary: Unemployed construction laborer with severe opioid use disorder on buprenorphine from an outside program, chronic hepatitis C, hypertension and recurrent depression who joins in 2022. In 2025 he has three episodes of MSSA endocarditis: aortic valve in March, a relapse with renal infarction in June, and mitral valve involvement with embolic stroke in December, each treated with six weeks of cefazolin. He recovers without deficit and reports no injecting since.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

42M establishing care. Wants a doctor closer to home than his old office; records release signed today.

What he wants from us: someone to keep his blood pressure and mood meds going and to know him if something goes wrong.

PMH (per pt, records requested):
- Opioid use disorder, severe. Gets buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg film daily from an outside office-based addiction program, sees them monthly with urine testing there. Has naloxone at home. Honest that he still injects "once in a while" - last time a few months ago. Uses new needles from the syringe service most of the time, not always.
- Chronic hepatitis C. Knows he has it. No liver symptoms.
- Hypertension on amlodipine 5 mg.
- Depression, recurrent - on sertraline 50 mg, says it takes the edge off.

PSH: ORIF right femur 2020. I&D left forearm abscess 2021.

Meds: bup/nlx 8/2 mg SL daily (program), naloxone 4 mg nasal PRN, amlodipine 5 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

FHx: father MI at 58, also had HTN. Mother T2DM. Brother with opioid use disorder.

SH: construction laborer, out of work right now. Lives alone, apartment in Amherst. Smokes 1 ppd x 20 yrs. Alcohol maybe 1-2 drinks a month. Injection opioid use as above, no other drugs he'll name.

ROS: tired a lot, sleep broken. No chest pain, no SOB, no fevers, no jaundice, no abdominal pain.

Exam: well-appearing, thin. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no LAD. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Ext: old healed scar left forearm, well-healed lateral R thigh scar; scattered old track marks antecubital fossae, no erythema or fluctuance. Neuro grossly normal.
PHQ-9 11. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. HTN - BP fine today on amlodipine 5. Continue.
2. MDD, recurrent, moderate - PHQ 11. Continue sertraline 50. He does not want counseling right now. Safety: denies SI.
3. OUD, severe, on buprenorphine - continue with his program; I'll be the backup. Naloxone in hand. Talked through safer injection basics when he does use.
4. Chronic HCV - viral load today, liver panel.
5. Tobacco - not ready to quit, open to talking again.
6. Prevention - HIV screen, hep B serologies (if nonimmune will vaccinate), lipids, A1c. Flu/COVID next month at nurse visit.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Rodney,

Your labs from Tuesday are in. Kidneys, liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol and sugar all look fine. HIV test is negative.

The hepatitis C viral load is positive (1,840,000), which fits with what you already knew - it means the virus is active in your blood. Your liver enzymes are normal right now.

You are not immune to hepatitis B, so I'd like to start the 2-shot hep B vaccine. We can do the first one with your flu shot in October.

Talk soon,
Primary care

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Faxed records received, 23 pages, from his previous primary care office, scanned to chart.

Summary sheet from that office:
Problems: opioid use disorder (on buprenorphine, outside prescriber); hepatitis C, chronic; hypertension; depression, recurrent; tobacco use.
Surgical: ORIF right femur (2020); incision and drainage, abscess L forearm (2021).
Medications: amlodipine 5 mg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; naloxone nasal spray PRN; buprenorphine-naloxone 8-2 mg film daily (outside).
Allergies: NKDA.
Last visit there about 8 months ago.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
In for flu, COVID booster and first Heplisav-B. Feeling well, no fever. Screening questions negative, NKDA.
Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Pfizer bivalent 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Heplisav-B 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, below flu site.
VIS given. Waited 15 min, fine. Dose 2 Heplisav due in 1 month - scheduled mid-November.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Heplisav-B #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Heplisav-B, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Tolerated first dose fine except sore arm. Series complete. No reaction during wait.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u BP and mood.

S: Doing "about the same." Takes amlodipine most days, misses maybe one a week. Sertraline daily. Still with the program, last visit there 2 wks ago, says urine was fine. Sleep still choppy. Smoking a pack a day, no change.

O: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Skin: no new injection sites seen, arms clean.
PHQ-9 9.

A/P:
- HTN: at goal. No change.
- Depression: PHQ down to 9. Continue sertraline 50. Gave the number for the counseling center again.
- OUD: stable on buprenorphine through program.
- HCV: reviewed viral load again, he understands it's active.
- Smoking: brief counseling, not ready.
- Hep B series done.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u.

Feels a bit better now that the days are longer. Taking amlodipine and sertraline. Program visits monthly, no use since before Christmas by his account. Still 1 ppd.

Vitals reviewed, BP 130s/80s. Heart regular, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema. Arms without new marks.
PHQ-9 8.

Plan
- HTN at goal on amlodipine 5.
- Depression improving, sertraline 50 - I'm taking over this Rx, sent 90 days with refills.
- New naloxone 2-pack sent, his old one expires this spring.
- OUD: continue program. Smoking: not ready, revisit.
- Annual physical in the fall.

documents.title: Care coordination letter - addiction treatment program
documents.author: addiction medicine
documents.body:
Re: Rodney Ferraro, DOB 10/20/1979

To the primary care physician:

This letter is to confirm that Mr. Ferraro is enrolled in our office-based opioid treatment program and is prescribed buprenorphine/naloxone 8 mg/2 mg sublingual film once daily. He attends monthly visits with toxicology monitoring. He has had occasional returns to use over the past year and remains engaged. He carries naloxone.

We would appreciate being notified of any hospitalizations or new controlled medications.

Allergies: NKDA.

Addiction medicine, outside office-based treatment program

documents.title: Missed appointment outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called re missed visit yesterday. Pt said he forgot, phone had been off. Offered video visit since he doesn't have a ride this month - booked 6/29 telehealth.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home in Amherst, ID confirmed by DOB.

Sorry about missing last time. Doing ok. Home BP cuff borrowed from a neighbor: readings he gives me 128-136 over low 80s. Mood steady, PHQ-9 9 by verbal. Taking meds. Still smoking, still with program.

Assessment: HTN controlled by home readings; depression stable on sertraline 50; OUD in treatment.
Plan: no changes. Physical in September, fasting not needed. Encouraged him to keep the program schedule.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

43M. Here for physical. No new complaints. Back pain? no. Breathing ok, morning cough from smoking.

Interval: missed June visit, did video instead. Still with the buprenorphine program; says he slipped once in the summer, injected, used a clean kit, no infection after.

Meds: amlodipine 5 daily, sertraline 50 daily, naloxone PRN, bup/nlx 8/2 daily (program).
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx unchanged: father MI 58 + HTN, mother T2DM, brother OUD.
SH: unemployed laborer, lives alone. 1 ppd x ~21 yrs. ETOH 1-2/month.

Exam: NAD. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx with some dental wear, no lesions. Neck: no thyromegaly or nodes. CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear, no wheeze. Abd: soft, NT, no organomegaly. Skin: old track scars, no active lesions. Ext: no edema. Neuro: nonfocal.
PHQ-9 7. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
- Health maintenance: PCV20 today (smoker, chronic liver infection) and Tdap - due. Colon screening starts at 45, next year. Not eligible for lung CT yet (age). Flu/COVID in October.
- HTN on amlodipine 5 - 152/85 on intake today, at goal at every other visit. Recheck next time, no change.
- Depression - best PHQ yet. Continue sertraline.
- OUD - continue program; naloxone current.
- HCV - chronic, liver tests today.
- Tobacco - 5 min counseling. Not ready. "Maybe when it gets cold."
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipid, A1c.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rodney - all your labs from the physical came back normal: kidneys, liver, blood count, cholesterol and sugar. Nothing to change. See you for flu/COVID shots next month.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; Moderna 2023-24 formula 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. No fever today, no prior reactions besides sore arm. VIS given, observed 15 minutes, left in good condition.

documents.title: Refill - sertraline
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called, pharmacy says sertraline has no refills. Checked - last Rx was 90 days x1 refill from March, so he's due. Also asked about naloxone, still has the 2-pack unused, ok.
Sertraline 50 mg #90 + 3 RF sent per protocol. Next visit due Feb - he'll call to book.
